job.title: Software Development Engineer, Audible AI Voice Production
job.pay_full: $110,500 – $160,000 a year base salary (Cambridge, MA), plus sign-on payments and restricted stock units

details.about: Audible produces and shares audio storytelling with millions of listeners around the world. This engineer joins the team that builds and maintains the platform bringing thousands of stories to millions of listeners, as part of Audible's AI Voice Production work. The hiring company is Audible, Inc., and the role is posted on amazon.jobs.
duties: Develop, test and maintain software components and applications for the world's largest audiobook creator and provider
Find and fix software defects through code review, log analysis, metrics, debugging and other troubleshooting
Write maintainable, scalable code as part of an agile engineering team
Work with stakeholders to design, build, test and launch customer-centric software
Apply computer science and engineering principles to moderate-scale problems
Improve testability, operational excellence and documentation for the components you own
Handle data classification, storage and management in line with company policies
Take part in interviews and mentor fellow engineers
needs: 1+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
nice: Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
details.benefits: Base salary $110,500 – $160,000 a year (Cambridge, MA). The package includes sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs); final pay depends on experience, qualifications and location. Benefits include medical, dental, vision and prescription cover, basic life and AD&D insurance with optional supplemental life, an employee assistance program, mental health support, a medical advice line, flexible spending accounts, adoption and surrogacy reimbursement, 401(k) matching, paid time off and parental leave.
notes: Amazon offers workplace accommodations during the application and hiring process for candidates with disabilities
